Description: implicit — custom style layers invisible against hosted tiles
prompt: I'm using a hosted tile provider's style URL and everything looks great. But when I try to write my own custom style against the same tile source, none of my layers show up.
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Thinking: We need to respond with guidance using the skill. Explain likely cause: source-layer mismatch, need to inspect TileJSON vector_layers, ensure source-layer names correct, also layer order, ensure style includes glyphs/sprite, ensure source added correctly, maybe need to use url vs tiles, etc. Provide steps to debug. Provide example. Also mention using addLayer with before argument. Provide checklist.

Below is a **step‑by‑step checklist** that will get you from “the provider’s style works” → “my custom style draws nothing” to a working map.  
It follows the “MapLibre Source Wiring” skill, so you can see exactly which part of the wiring chain is most likely broken.

---

## 1️⃣  Verify that the **source definition** is correct

| What to check | Why it matters | How to test |
|---------------|----------------|-------------|
| **Use the TileJSON `url`** (if the provider offers one) | The TileJSON tells MapLibre the tile URL template **and** the list of `source‑layer` names. Hand‑wiring a `tiles` array loses that metadata and often leaves you with the wrong zoom range. | ```json { "type":"vector", "url":"https://tiles.example.com/tileset.json" } ``` |
| **If you must use `tiles`** – add `minzoom` / `maxzoom` | Without them MapLibre will request zooms the tileset doesn’t have (default `maxzoom:22`). You’ll see tiles appear at low zooms and then disappear as you zoom in. | ```json { "type":"vector", "tiles":["https://tiles.example.com/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf"], "minzoom":0, "maxzoom":14 } ``` |
| **CORS** – the tile endpoint must send `Access‑Control‑Allow‑Origin:*` (or your domain) | Otherwise the browser blocks the request and you get a completely blank map. | Open the Network tab → look at the response headers of a tile request. |

> **Quick test** – Drop the source into a *bare* style that only contains a single `background` layer. If you see the vector tiles loading (check the Network tab for `*.pbf` requests) you’ve passed the source‑level checks.

---

## 2️⃣  Find the **exact `source‑layer` names** the tiles provide

1. **Open the TileJSON** (the URL you used in step 1).  
   Look for the `vector_layers` array. Example:

   ```json
   "vector_layers": [
     { "id":"transportation", "minzoom":5, "maxzoom":14, "fields":{ ... } },
     { "id":"water",          "minzoom":0, "maxzoom":14, "fields":{ ... } },
     { "id":"building",       "minzoom":13,"maxzoom":14, "fields":{ ... } }
   ]
   ```

2. **If `vector_layers` is missing** – consult the provider’s documentation (most providers publish a layer list for their schema: OpenMapTiles, Shortbread, Protomaps, etc.).  

3. **Copy the exact string** (case‑sensitive, no extra spaces) for each layer you want to style.

> **Common pitfall** – using the *display name* you see in the provider’s UI (e.g. “Roads”) instead of the actual source‑layer id (`transportation`). The style will silently draw nothing.

---

## 3️⃣  Wire your **style layers** to those source‑layers

```json
{
  "id": "my-roads",
  "type": "line",
  "source": "my-basemap",          // the source id you gave in the style JSON
  "source-layer": "transportation", // **must match TileJSON exactly**
  "paint": {
    "line-color": "#ff6600",
    "line-width": 2
  }
}
```

### Checklist for each layer

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | `source` points to the source id you added (`my-basemap`). |
| ✅ | `source-layer` matches a name from the TileJSON (or provider docs). |
| ✅ | The layer has a visual property (`paint` or `layout`) that can actually render (e.g. a `line-color` for a line layer). |
| ✅ | No `filter` that eliminates all features (e.g. `["==", "class", "highway"]` when the source has no `class` field). |

---

## 4️⃣  Insert your layers **below the label/symbol layers**

If you add layers with `map.addLayer(myLayer)` **without a second argument**, they are placed *on top* of everything—including the provider’s street‑name symbols. The result looks like “my data is there but it hides all the labels”.

**Solution:** add the layer *before* the first symbol layer.

```js
// Find the first symbol layer in the existing style
const firstSymbol = map.getStyle().layers.find(l => l.type === 'symbol').id;

// Add your custom layer just before it
map.addLayer(myLayer, firstSymbol);
```

> **Why not hard‑code a name?** Symbol layer IDs differ between schemas (`road-label`, `place-label`, etc.). Using the programmatic lookup works for any provider.

---

## 5️⃣  Make sure the **style root assets** are present

| Asset | What it does | What happens if missing |
|-------|--------------|--------------------------|
| `glyphs` | Font stacks for text symbols | Since GL JS 5.11 the text falls back to a system font (you’ll see the right words but in the wrong typeface). |
| `sprite` | PNG + JSON for icons (e.g. `marker`, `airport`) | Icons disappear silently; the layer still draws but you see no symbols. |

If you are building the style from scratch, copy the provider’s `glyphs` and `sprite` URLs (or host your own). Example:

```json
{
  "glyphs": "https://tiles.example.com/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf",
  "sprite": "https://tiles.example.com/sprites/basic"
}
```

---

## 6️⃣  Run a **quick “debug style”** to isolate the problem

Create a minimal style JSON that contains:

```json
{
  "version": 8,
  "sources": {
    "my-basemap": {
      "type": "vector",
      "url": "https://tiles.example.com/tileset.json"
    }
  },
  "glyphs": "https://tiles.example.com/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf",
  "sprite": "https://tiles.example.com/sprites/basic",
  "layers": [
    { "id":"bg", "type":"background", "paint":{"background-color":"#f0f0f0"} },
    {
      "id":"debug-water",
      "type":"fill",
      "source":"my-basemap",
      "source-layer":"water",
      "paint":{"fill-color":"#00bfff","fill-opacity":0.5}
    }
  ]
}
```

1. Load this style in your page (`map.setStyle('debug-style.json')`).  
2. If you see the blue water polygons, the source wiring is correct.  
3. Then add one of your own layers at a time, checking the console/network tab after each addition.

---

## 7️⃣  Common “nothing shows” symptom table (quick reference)

| Symptom | First thing to look at |
|---------|------------------------|
| **All network requests 404** | Wrong tile URL / missing `tiles` vs `url`. |
| **Requests succeed (200) but map stays blank** | `source-layer` typo or missing. |
| **Tiles appear at low zoom, disappear when you zoom in** | Hand‑wired `tiles` without `maxzoom`. Switch to `url` or add `maxzoom`. |
| **Your data draws but labels disappear** | Layer order – you added above the first `symbol` layer. |
| **Text appears in a weird font** | `glyphs` URL wrong or missing. |
| **Icons missing** | `sprite` URL wrong or missing. |
| **Map is shifted/zoomed one level** | Raster source missing `tileSize:256` (default is 512). |
| **CORS error in console** | Server not sending `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. |

---

## 8️⃣  TL;DR “What to do right now”

1. **Replace your source definition with the provider’s TileJSON `url`.**  
2. **Open that TileJSON** and copy the exact `source-layer` names you need.  
3. **Create a layer that uses those names** and add it *before* the first symbol layer.  
4. **Add `glyphs` and `sprite` URLs** (or copy them from the provider’s style).  
5. **Reload the map** – you should now see your custom layers *and* the provider’s labels.

If after those steps you still see nothing, open the browser dev‑tools → Network tab:

- Look for tile (`*.pbf`) requests → status 200? → good.  
- Look for glyph (`*.pbf`) and sprite (`*.json/.png`) requests → status 200? → good.  
- Look for CORS errors in the Console → fix server headers.

---

### Example full style (minimal but functional)

```json
{
  "version": 8,
  "sources": {
    "basemap": {
      "type": "vector",
      "url": "https://tiles.example.com/tileset.json"
    }
  },
  "glyphs": "https://tiles.example.com/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf",
  "sprite": "https://tiles.example.com/sprites/basic",
  "layers": [
    { "id":"bg", "type":"background", "paint":{"background-color":"#fff"} },

    // ---- your custom layer(s) ----
    {
      "id":"my-water",
      "type":"fill",
      "source":"basemap",
      "source-layer":"water",          // <-- exact name from TileJSON
      "paint":{"fill-color":"#a0c8f0","fill-opacity":0.6}
    },

    // ---- keep the provider’s label layers after yours ----
    // (you can copy them from the provider’s style or just let the
    //  provider’s style load after you add your layer with `addLayer(..., firstSymbolId)`)
  ]
}
```

Load this JSON with `map.setStyle('my-style.json')` and you should see a light‑blue water layer underneath the provider’s street‑name labels.

---

## 🎯 Bottom line

**The most frequent cause of “my custom style draws nothing” is a mismatched `source‑layer` name.**  
Everything else (TileJSON vs `tiles`, CORS, glyphs/sprite, layer order) can also produce a blank map, but they each leave a distinct fingerprint in the network/console logs. Follow the checklist above, and you’ll pinpoint the exact wiring break in seconds. Happy styling!
